stories.headline: OpenAI tests defenses against adversarial model distillation

source.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
source.scope: Reviewed the complete research article, including adaptive extraction attacks, the evaluation setup, reported defense results, threat assumptions and the limitation that the evidence comes from internal tests.
source.freshness_reason: Published two days before the edition; retained after complete original-source review and lane comparison.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete research article, including adaptive extraction attacks, the evaluation setup, reported defense results, threat assumptions and the limitation that the evidence comes from internal tests.

stories.summary: OpenAI describes an adaptive evaluation for adversarial distillation, where an attacker repeatedly queries a model to reproduce valuable behavior. The research compares defenses against changing extraction strategies instead of one fixed attack. Results come from internal tests, so the reported gains establish a security method and threat model rather than independent proof of broad protection.
stories.why_it_matters: Model providers can evaluate extraction defenses against attackers that adapt after each failure. Define the protected capability, measure utility loss for normal users, vary the adversary’s strategy and require independent reproduction before treating one internal benchmark as durable security evidence.
stories.image_alt_intent: An adaptive extraction loop tests a model defense while separate gauges track attacker success, normal-user utility and independent reproduction.
stories.related_coverage: Selected after complete original-source review and comparison with current security and model-engineering candidates.

stories.headline: A large multi-agent study exposes research coordination limits

source.title: A Society of AI Scientists
source.scope: Reviewed the original manuscript page and full paper, including 936 agents across 35 laboratories, the twelve-week protocol, coordination mechanisms, reported outputs, audit limitations and the absence of independent replication.
source.freshness_reason: Published three days before the edition; admitted as a qualified original-paper fallback after full methods and limitations review.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the original manuscript page and full paper, including 936 agents across 35 laboratories, the twelve-week protocol, coordination mechanisms, reported outputs, audit limitations and the absence of independent replication.

stories.summary: The alphaXiv paper reports a twelve-week study coordinating 936 agents across 35 simulated laboratories to produce research artifacts. Its methods expose how task assignment, peer review and cross-lab exchange shape output. The scale is unusual, but the platform controls the experiment and independent replication, external code audit and durable scientific impact remain unestablished.
stories.why_it_matters: Research-agent teams can borrow the study’s separation of roles, review stages and shared records without copying its scale. Preserve prompts, code, failed attempts and reviewer decisions, then test whether independent experts can reproduce one result before claiming autonomous scientific progress.
stories.image_alt_intent: Thirty-five simulated laboratories exchange reviewed research artifacts while an external audit gate remains visibly unresolved.
stories.related_coverage: Selected as the edition’s original-paper item after full methods, results and limitations review.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Ignite announcement and linked model-card evidence covering seven models, reported benchmark comparisons, pricing, availability, intended uses, operator-reported limits and the distinction between benchmark cost and completed-work cost.

stories.summary: Microsoft announced seven models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, speech and decision routing, emphasizing benchmark quality per dollar. The article and linked model cards also describe availability and intended-use limits. Because the comparisons and prices are operator-selected, knowledge teams should test completed tasks, retries, review time and failure costs on representative work before switching.
stories.why_it_matters: Procurement teams can turn price-performance claims into a task-level test. Freeze representative cases, define acceptable outputs, record retries and human review, include failure recovery and compare total completed-work cost instead of multiplying token prices by optimistic benchmark scores.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete practitioner guide covering model substitution, workflow boundaries, provider-specific behavior, fallback design, evaluation, data handling and the limits of treating models as interchangeable.

stories.summary: Zapier argues that workflow owners should separate a business process from any one model provider, then compare substitutes against stable inputs and acceptance checks. The guide covers routing, fallback and data-handling differences while warning that models are not interchangeable. Its examples are vendor-authored, so teams should validate quality, latency, permissions and failure behavior independently.
stories.why_it_matters: Operations teams can reduce switching risk by freezing representative inputs, expected outputs and approval boundaries before changing providers. Compare quality, latency, cost, retention rules and fallback behavior on the same cases, then keep a tested rollback instead of assuming API compatibility means workflow equivalence.

stories.headline: Turn one Slack agent workflow into a bounded reusable Skill

source.title: Bring agents into your workflows
source.scope: Reviewed the complete product workflow guide covering triggers, channel and document context, agent steps, human review, permissions, exception handling and measurable workflow outcomes.
source.freshness_reason: Four-day fallback retained because the full guide supports a distinct reusable noncoding procedure.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete product workflow guide covering triggers, channel and document context, agent steps, human review, permissions, exception handling and measurable workflow outcomes.

stories.summary: Slack shows how agents can enter Workflow Builder after a defined trigger, use approved channel or document context and return a draft for human review. The guide is first-party product evidence, not proof of general productivity. A reusable Skill should therefore bind the trigger, permitted sources, output format, exception path and measurable result.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams can convert one recurring Slack request into a reviewable Skill. Define the trigger, restrict context, specify the draft format, route exceptions to a named owner and measure one outcome such as resolved requests or review time before expanding automation.
stories.image_alt_intent: A Slack workflow trigger passes approved context into a reusable agent Skill, then routes drafts and exceptions to a named human reviewer.

audience_fit.practical_action: Define one trigger, approved context, output format, exception owner and measurable workflow result.
audience_fit.review_action: Test known normal and exception cases, inspect every source and keep final approval with the named reviewer.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable Slack Skill that returns consistent drafts and visible exceptions for human approval.

stories.summary: Microsoft’s Copilot SDK 2.0 architecture separates agent sessions, journals and tenant boundaries while exposing tools and approval points to applications. candidates.disposition_reason: The complete original security article documents an adaptive extraction threat model, evaluation setup, defense results and explicit internal-evidence limits.
The full original paper supplies a twelve-week multi-agent research protocol, coordination mechanisms, reported artifacts and clearly bounded replication limitations.
The complete model-family announcement and linked model cards support a bounded task-economics evaluation while keeping operator-selected benchmark limitations explicit.
The complete practitioner guide supports stable workflow tests, provider substitution, fallback design and data-handling comparisons without claiming interchangeability.
The full Workflow Builder guide supports the edition’s sole reusable noncoding Skill with bounded context, review, exceptions and a measurable outcome.
The complete architecture article exposes session, journal, tenant, tool and approval boundaries that nontechnical workflow owners can test directly.
The complete scientific announcement was substantive, but this edition’s technical lanes favored an explicit adaptive-security evaluation and an original multi-agent methods paper.
The asynchronous agent pattern was useful engineering evidence, but it overlapped recent agent-orchestration coverage and offered less distinct reader value.
The harness-adapter experiment was fully reviewed but appeared in the immediately preceding edition, so exact source novelty correctly overrode recency.
The deployed calling history was substantive but appeared in the preceding edition and could not satisfy exact-source novelty for November 22.

fallback_decisions.why_selected_over_recent_options: The adversarial-distillation article adds a distinct adaptive extraction threat model and defense evaluation; the other current sources concern orchestration and harness portability already covered recently.

The society-of-scientists paper provides a full multi-agent research protocol and coordination evidence; the comparison sources cover biological prediction and asynchronous orchestration rather than scientific team behavior.
The Microsoft model-family release supports a distinct task-economics procurement test with linked model-card limits; the newer engineering sources do not answer that knowledge-work cost decision.
The Zapier guide uniquely addresses provider substitution, stable acceptance tests and rollback behavior; asynchronous agents and deployed calling histories concern different workflow mechanisms.
The Slack guide enables the edition’s sole reusable noncoding Skill with a trigger, bounded context, exception owner and measurable outcome; the engineering alternatives do not.
The Copilot architecture makes sessions, journals, tenant boundaries and approval points inspectable for workflow owners; the current alternatives lack that complete control-map decision.

programs.source_scope: Reviewed the complete 10:25 TED talk in which Brian Janous explains community opposition to AI data centers and proposes mechanisms for sharing local economic benefits, with his industry role treated as a disclosed perspective.
programs.reader_question: Use the talk to structure a data-center decision: list local power, water and tax costs; identify who receives the benefits; require public assumptions; and compare community-benefit mechanisms before treating construction jobs or regional growth claims as settled.
programs.distinct_contribution: This program supports a distinct reader decision: Examine who bears the local costs of AI data centers and how host communities could share their economic benefits.

programs.source_scope: Reviewed the complete 11:34 educational program and transcript explaining classification, features, labeled data, decision trees, support-vector machines, neural networks, narrow AI and reinforcement learning through concrete examples.
programs.reader_question: Use the explainer to give a team shared vocabulary before evaluating a modern system. Ask which features, labels, objective and feedback loop produce each output, then supplement the nine-year-old foundation with current evidence about model limits, data provenance and oversight.
programs.distinct_contribution: This program supports a distinct reader decision: Build a conceptual map of classification, features, labeled data, decision trees, neural networks and reinforcement learning.

programs.source_scope: Reviewed the complete 1:47:42 publisher transcript and chapter structure, including capability leadership, national-security threats, safety policy, institutional capacity and explicit disagreements.
programs.reader_question: Use the discussion to stress-test an AI policy proposal: identify the protected capability, credible threat, enforcement mechanism, responsible institution and evidence that would change the policy. Keep strategic urgency separate from proof that a chosen safeguard works.
programs.distinct_contribution: This episode supports a distinct reader decision: Separate strategic AI policy arguments from measurable safety evidence and enforceable controls.

programs.distinct_contribution: This episode supports a distinct reader decision: Build a reviewable bill of materials for an AI-assisted software delivery path.
